lines.text: People who have never met want to train one AI model together. Why would any of them trust the others?
lines.source: Ural and Yoshigoe 2023, Sec. I, IV (collaborative and federated training among parties that do not trust each other)

lines.text: Someone can slip in bad data and still collect a reward. And the finished model keeps no record of what went into it.
lines.source: Sec. IV-A (data poisoning; a trained model carries no record of its training)

lines.text: A blockchain is a shared notebook that nobody can quietly rewrite. Write every step of the training into it, and tampering stops being invisible.
lines.source: Sec. II-A, IV-A (immutability; recording the training transactions gives a tamper-evident record)

lines.text: The data itself never goes into the notebook. It stays with its owner. Only the model's updates are shared.
lines.source: Sec. IV-A (data stays on the owners' devices; only model parameters are shared and updated on the chain)

lines.text: Ordinary blockchains agree by burning electricity on puzzles whose answers are worth nothing. So researchers aimed that effort at something useful: training the model. Whoever trains the best one writes the next page.
lines.source: Sec. II-B, IV-C (proof of work; proof of useful work; Proof of Learning: the miner with the best model writes the next block)

lines.text: Now the electricity buys a model. But it raises a hard question: how do you prove the training was real?
lines.source: Sec. II-B (critiques of Proof-of-Learning; verifying claimed training)

lines.text: Then, the incentives. A contract pays each contributor by how much their data improved the model. Send in junk, and you lose money.
lines.source: Sec. IV-B (Sharing Updatable Models: the balance moves by the loss before an update minus the loss after it)

lines.text: You also put down a deposit. Good data gets it back. Bad data forfeits it.
lines.source: Sec. IV-B (deposit, refund, take; in simulation the bad agents deplete their balance)

lines.text: And when people actually built these systems, the measurements were sobering. More participants made the model more accurate, and the network slower. More privacy cost accuracy.
lines.source: Sec. IV-B (DeepChain on Corda with MNIST: accuracy up, throughput down, time up as parties join; LearningChain: privacy against accuracy)

lines.text: So our survey ends on the open problems: speed, energy, and rules of agreement designed for learning rather than for currency.
lines.source: Sec. V (challenges: scalability, energy, consensus designed for machine learning)

lines.text: One of those problems, proving that training really happened, became my doctoral research.
lines.source: the author's path (old lab film, closing line)
